newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Petrobras, Volkswagen biggest Brazil firms in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras, Volkswagen biggest Brazil firms in 1996.

text.p: State oil firm Petrobras and Volkswagen retained their rankings as Brazil's largest state and private firms respectively in 1996 in terms of sales, Exame magazine said in its annual survey.
The Forbes-like ranking of Brazil's 500 top firms, due to hit newstands later this month, said Petrobras raked in receipts of $23.58 billion, up 8.9 percent from 1995.

Meanwhile, Volkswagen's local unit was first among private firms for the third year in a row, taking in $9.21 billion in sales revenue in 1996, a rise of 24.8 percent over the prior year, the magazine said.

Among private firms, General Motors was second again with sales of $7.23 billion, up 10.7 percent, and Fiat Automoveis held onto third place despite a 3.4 percent drop in receipts to $6.14 billion, it said.
The highest-ranking private Brazilian-owned firm was beverage and cigarette maker Souza Cruz, again at No. 4, with sales revenue of $5.79 billion, down 0.1 percent from 1995.
The following private firms also made Exame's top 10 list:
5 - Shell with $5.62 billion, up 3.8 percent.
6 - Ford, which jumped from 16th the prior year, with $4.77 billion, a rise of 66.2 percent.
7 - Carrefour, down from sixth in 1995, with $4.51 billion, up 6.8 percent.
8 - Nestle, up from ninth with $4.19 billion, a 21.6 percent rise.
9 - Ipiranga, down from seventh with $4.13 billion, up 4.7 percent.
10 - Gessy Lever with $3.5 billion, up 1.7 percent.
Among the 50 largest state-owned companies, Petrobras BR Distribuidora again came in second with receipts of $9.14 billion, a rise of 4.6 percent from 1995.
Eletropaulo was third with $5.69 billion, a rise of 15.4 percent, and Telesp rose to fourth from fifth in 1995 with a 37.9 percent rise in receipts to $4.78 billion in 1996.
The magazine provided the following ranking for state firms:
5 - Cesp, down from fourth, with $3.6 billion, up 3.4 percent.
6 - Furnas with $3.25 billion, up 6.7 percent.
7 - Correios e Telegrafos, unranked last year, with $2.6 billion, up 24.8 percent.
9 - Sabesp with $2.42 billion, up 12.7 percent.
10 - Embratel with $2.36 billion, up 19.8 percent.

Exame's survey, conducted by the University of Sao Paulo, said total sales for the 500 largest private companies in Brazil were $280.3 billion and profits fell 4.15 percent to $7.6 billion in 1996 versus the prior year.
Ten years ago, in an atmosphere of high interest rates and high inflation, profits were double, or $14.6 billion.
Mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce, which was privatized last month, posted a net profit of $608 million in 1996 while state-owned telecom Telesp earned $870 million.
((-- Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 2485413))
